Neither ever pushes, and both report that they pushed nothing, so a lost container loses both commits. The same rule blocks a worker landing a merged tree, whose `origin/main..main` range always holds other agents' commits (and a merge commit that no `git commit` of its own printed). That worker can never push by the rule. The skill also gives no step for a rejected push or a stale `origin/main` (no fetch), and no way to wait 'shortly' when `sleep N; cmd` is refused.

findings.consequence: After `git mv XXXName.fss Name.fss`, the old path is in neither the index nor the work tree, so `git add -- ... XXXName.fss` fails ('pathspec did not match') and the `&&` commits nothing. If the worker names only the new paths, the commit adds Name.* and leaves XXXName.fss and XXXName.test in HEAD, with their deletion still staged. The landed tree then holds the old XXX test, which now passes and so turns red in the gate, beside a duplicate of the program. findings.what: For the XXX run file, 'Never use run_out_contains=PASS'. The promoted Name.test then has `run_out_contains=PASS`. 'A run-time pair keeps its stem, and becomes three files' (it already had three: .fss and two .test). Name.test adds `link`, although NameLink.test also links.
findings.consequence: Small doubt about whether PASS is allowed, what 'stem' is, and whether NameLink.test stays. The worker may drop it or leave out `link`.

findings.what: '$L close N --commit HASH --test NAME ... Run it once that commit is in HEAD.' committing.md: 'Commit what you write to the record, such as a ledger row, with the work that it records.'
findings.consequence: The close cannot go in the fix's commit, because the hash is not known yet. The worker has to decide on a second commit, which the skill seems to discourage.

findings.what: 'The newest gate summary has the exact counts and times', but summary.txt holds tests, failures, errors and skipped only (gate.md 7). 'Read the verdict in the last line: BUILD SUCCESSFUL', but ant ends with 'Total time:' and run_bg appends EXIT=.
findings.consequence: The worker looks for times that are not in the summary, and for the verdict in the wrong line.

findings.what: The seds replace /home/user/fortress with $PWD only in microgpt-phase.sh. run-subset.sh gets only its OUT and LADDER_ROOT lines rewritten.
findings.consequence: If run-subset.sh holds the main tree's path elsewhere, a gate in a worktree (a merged tree) runs the main checkout's code in the ladder and reports a ladder that is not this tree's. A cold reader cannot tell.

findings.what: 'Do not compare the output of a whole run of tests with a saved copy ... The gate's ladder regression is the one exception.'
findings.consequence: Step 5's gate_compare compares the run's summary with the last landed summary, a second exception that this line denies. The worker may doubt step 5.

assumptions.assumed: `git add` fails on a path that `git mv` already removed from the index, while `git commit -- <old path>` still commits its deletion.
assumptions.why: To check whether the skill's one-command commit works for a promotion by `git mv`.

assumptions.assumed: All worktrees share the repository's refs, so `origin/main` updates when any local agent pushes, and nobody pushes main from elsewhere (no `git fetch` needed before `git log origin/main..main`).
assumptions.why: The push rule relies on `origin/main..main` being current, and says nothing of fetch or a rejected push.
assumptions.source: prior knowledge of git worktrees; guess about the workflow

assumptions.assumed: A worker on main is in the main checkout, because a worktree cannot check out main while the main checkout has it.
assumptions.why: To tell which tree 'If you work on main' applies to.

assumptions.assumed: The shell functions in climb-batch-workflow.js can be turned into bash by unescaping the JS string literals (for example by evaluating the array with node and printing it), then defined or sourced in each Bash call, and exported for a run_bg child.
assumptions.why: Gate steps 5 and 7 need them, and the skill gives no method.

assumptions.assumed: run-subset.sh, classify.py, microgpt-phase.sh and microgpt-phase.py run from $D with no arguments (python3 for the .py files).
assumptions.why: Gate ladder step 2 names only their order.

assumptions.assumed: gate_compare tolerates a rise in test counts from added tests and reports only drops or failures.
assumptions.why: A merged tree adds tests, and the skill says each printed line makes the gate red.

assumptions.assumed: Gate step 3's copy of the caches is unconditional; only the library order depends on the 'started again' line.
assumptions.why: The sentence order allows both readings.
assumptions.source: guess from the layout of step 3

assumptions.assumed: For a merged tree whose merge changed a compiler-library file without changing Java, the gate worker must also take the 'After an edit of the library' step before the atomic runs and the ladder.
assumptions.why: Otherwise the kept caches hold the old library's jars.
assumptions.source: inference from build-and-caches.md 118-123; the gate does not say it

assumptions.assumed: tmp/gate should be emptied, or be new, before a gate run.
assumptions.why: cp -a into an existing ladder-caches nests the copy, and old raw outputs mix in.

assumptions.assumed: 'Passes' in 'Changed for one run so that it passes' means the program behaves as if fixed (for a run-time pair: remove or guard the failing part so the run exits 0 and prints REACHED), after which the harness reports the XXX test red.
assumptions.why: The skill's two examples fit compile-time XXX tests only.

assumptions.assumed: The scenario's 'XXX test first, promoted after the fix' means the brief told the worker to record the defect as XXX first. Promotion then still renames before the code edit, and the plain test's failure on the base is shown through old-fortress.sh junit with both .test files named.
assumptions.why: The skill says a repaired defect needs no XXX stage, and that promotion renames before the fix.

assumptions.assumed: old-fortress.sh junit accepts several .test paths in one call, so the link file runs with the run file.
assumptions.why: The run-time pair must run in one call; worktrees.md shows only one file.

assumptions.assumed: A private caches folder for a hand compile or run is set through FORTRESS_CACHES and `-Dfortress.caches` inside JAVA_FLAGS, and must first get the library's jars (by a copy of default_repository/caches or the library order).
assumptions.why: The compiler.md quick loop names both settings but not where they go or what the folder needs.

assumptions.assumed: How to put a scratch class directory first on bin/fortress's class path (a CLASSPATH variable, or a hand-built java line from bin/fortress_classpath).
assumptions.why: The quick loop requires it.

assumptions.assumed: A run-time fix in runtimeSystem/ falls under 'every other change' (own tests only, plus atomic runs if near transactions or the class loader), and OverloadSet counts as the code generator.
assumptions.why: The whole-suite rule names the checker, walk, shared phases and the code generator only.

assumptions.assumed: For a junit.sh log the worker must grep `OK (` / `FAILURES!!!` itself, because wait_for's grep does not show them.
assumptions.why: wait_for prints only ant verdicts and EXIT, and junit.sh always exits 0.

assumptions.assumed: Commit messages with the footer are written with several -m flags or a heredoc, with a blank line before the trailers.
assumptions.why: The skill's command shows a single -m.

assumptions.assumed: 'Say so in its message' (original-tree edits) has no set wording.
assumptions.why: No format is given.

assumptions.why: The two sources conflict, and only the footer conflict is addressed.
assumptions.source: guess from 'whatever footer Claude Code suggests'

assumptions.assumed: The ledger close (`$L close`) goes in a second commit after the fix commit.
assumptions.why: It needs the fix's hash in HEAD.

assumptions.assumed: The commit that lands a gate summary should contain only the gate folder, because the gate validity check assumes 'the commit that landed the newest summary changed nothing that the gate reads'.
assumptions.why: This is stated as a fact, not as a rule.

assumptions.assumed: `gate-baseline/` is under explorations/compile-ladder/.
assumptions.why: gate.md names it without a path.

assumptions.assumed: The new climb-batch-<N> folder takes the next number after the highest existing one.
assumptions.why: Not stated.

assumptions.assumed: Each `fortress compile` in the library order is run under one run_bg, with each exit code recorded separately.
assumptions.why: Exit codes must be quoted if a jar is missing, and wait_for shows only the last EXIT.

assumptions.assumed: Waiting 'shortly' before re-running `git log origin/main..main` uses wait_for-like polling, since `sleep N; cmd` is refused.

terms: XXX test: used both for a .test file whose name has the XXX prefix (every command must fail) and for a component whose name contains XXX (its link or compile exception is expected whatever the .test file's name) (tests-writing.md 72-74 vs 106-108)
green / red: defined in tests-writing.md for a harness report on one test, but used earlier for a whole tree ('Take the tree that you start from as green', SKILL.md 162) and for the gate (gate.md 3)

pass / fail: used for the program and for the test; for an XXX test, 'see it fail through the harness' (SKILL.md 160) means the harness reports green, and 'changed so that it passes' (tests-writing.md 115) means the harness reports red
plain: a name without XXX, a non-refusal test ('A plain test is green if walk refuses...'), a non-generic declaration, and 'plain Java values'
tree vs original tree: 'tree' is a checkout (build-and-caches.md 3), 'original tree' is the team's part of the repository (SKILL.md 16); both appear in the same rules
library: the interpreter's library (the 'library area', library.md) and the compiler's library (the 'library order', 'library jars'); 'After an edit of the library' covers both
climb-batch-N: a literal folder name (tests-running.md 110) vs climb-batch-<N> / climb-batch-* for the numbered batch folders (gate.md 9, tests-running.md 25)
stem (tests-writing.md 125): never defined
ladder tables (gate.md 9) and ladder.tsv (gate.md 98): never defined; the skill does not say which ladder outputs they are
pristine (gate.md 36): copy of the caches whose use is never explained
gate-baseline/ (gate.md 9): location never given
last_landed_summary, gate_summary, gate_compare, ladder_compare, mg_phases: used as commands, never described beyond their location in a JS file
merged tree: never used or defined; the skill says nothing on how to gate or land a merge
suite: testFast/testSystem, 'track/suite' rows of the summary, and 'the test suite' in general (SKILL.md 160)
code state (tests-running.md 9): defined, but whether a merge is 'an edit of code' is not said
decision not taken and point to report: used in SKILL.md 171 before records.md and exploring.md define them
run test / link test / compile test: used as kinds without definition (implied by 'each present command is one JUnit case')
verdict / verdict lines: the ant BUILD line, JUnit's 'OK (n tests)'/'FAILURES!!!', mg-run's 'VERDICT:' and wait_for's grep output
wall (code-generator wall): used in tests-writing.md 105 before compiler.md defines it (pointer given)
base / base build / base's code / old code: four near-synonyms for related but different things
REACHED: a convention introduced only inside the run-time XXX recipe

findings.what: interpreter.md:58 says 'To check the model after a library change, run explorations/coordinator/tools/mg-run.sh <work-dir> <label> [threads]'. tests-running.md:68 says 'After every other change, run only your own tests ... This includes an edit of either library'. SKILL.md:164 says to run a whole suite only where tests-running.md asks, and nowhere else. library.md, the part a library worker loads, never mentions mg-run.sh, and SKILL.md:184 files 'the microGPT check' under the interpreter area. MicroGPT 'runs only under walk ... never in the gate' (interpreter.md:58), and the gate only compiles the microGPT components against the compiler's library (gate.md:68).
findings.consequence: A worker editing Library/*.fss under walk who loads library.md, tests-writing.md and tests-running.md concludes it should run only its own tests. It never runs mg-run.sh, and nothing else ever runs the model under walk with the interpreter's library, so a library edit that breaks microGPT lands unseen. A worker who does find interpreter.md:58 cannot tell whether the check is required or optional ('To check the model' reads both ways), and it does not know where <work-dir> goes or what [threads] defaults to.

findings.what: Step 2 says to see the test fail 'through the harness (harness-one.sh or junit.sh)', and adds: 'If your tree already holds the fix, run the base's code through explorations/coordinator/tools/old-fortress.sh'. worktrees.md:51-62 shows old-fortress.sh running bin/fortress directly (compile/run/walk/junit), not the walk harness. worktrees.md:64-67 gives a separate recipe for walk tests on old code: 'FORTRESS_HOME=<base-build> <base-build>/explorations/compile-ladder/rung-inference-walk/harness-one.sh ...'.
findings.consequence: A walk Java fixer, or a library worker whose edit is already in its tree, follows tests-writing.md and runs 'old-fortress.sh <base> <tmp> X.fss', which is a direct walk run and not the harness. The 'see it fail through the harness' rule (SKILL.md:160) is then not met: the direct run uses another heap and does not apply the harness's fail/FAIL output rule or the .test keys for load refusals. The worker either reports a non-harness failure or spends time reconciling the two files.

findings.what: 'Your brief says whether you commit and push, and on which branch. If it says nothing, commit on your current branch, and push it.' SKILL.md:41 defines landing as committing to main and pushing main, and the gate as the 'Full check of a tree before it lands'. gate.md:15 says 'If [your brief] does not ask, run only your own tests.'
findings.consequence: A worker whose current branch is main and whose brief is silent commits and pushes main (with the three pushes at lines 42-47). By the skill's own definition that lands the tree without a gate. The walk Java fixer, who has run only harness-one and testSystem, is the most likely to do this.

findings.what: Two actions due before the edit sit only in records.md. ''ledger-find:WORDS' ... Run it when you meet a defect, before you investigate it.' 'Before you edit a file of the original tree, list the ledger rows that cite it: python3 explorations/coordinator/tools/ledger.py find --cites FILE'. SKILL.md lists records.md last in 'the order that work meets them' and describes it as 'What every report holds ...'. SKILL.md:197 says only 'Every report takes the form in records.md'.
findings.consequence: Workers who read parts in the listed order open records.md at report time, after they have investigated and edited. The walk fixer misses an existing ledger row or XXX test for its defect, which tests-writing.md:119 needs for promotion, and duplicates or misses work. The library and spec workers skip the --cites check. Line 67 also does not say what to do with the rows it lists (read them, cite them, update them).

findings.what: The rule that tells a walk fixer where a fix belongs is in compiler.md:21: walk turns off the coercion, chained-comparison, assignment, case/typecase/ascription desugarings and evaluates those nodes in Evaluator.java, so 'If walk is wrong there, fix the evaluator'. interpreter.md points to it only in its last section, 'After an edit here'. That section also points to compiler.md 'What the two paths share' for a report duty (say which path you fixed and whether the other has the same defect). compiler.md is not in SKILL.md:197's example list for an interpreter fix.
findings.consequence: A walk fixer chasing, say, a wrong coercion or typecase result finds the desugarer under compiler/ (a shared phase) and fixes it there. The change does not reach walk, because walk switches that desugaring off, or it changes only the compiled path. The pointer arrives only after the edit. The fixer may also omit the 'other path has the same defect?' line from its report.

findings.what: 'To see what an early phase makes of a program, stop after that phase: parse, disambiguate, grammar, desugar or typecheck' and ''unparse' ... Use it to see what a desugaring made.' Then: 'Walk and test call Shell.useInterpreterLibraries(). Every other command calls useCompilerLibraries(). Each call ... sets the desugaring switches.' interpreter.md:20 warns only about typecheck.
findings.consequence: A walk fixer who uses 'bin/fortress desugar P.fss' or 'unparse' to inspect walk's tree gets the tree built against the compiler's prelude, with the compiled path's desugaring switches. That tree is not what walk interprets, so the fixer debugs the wrong tree or concludes a desugaring ran when walk turns it off. The skill gives no command that shows walk's own post-phase tree, apart from the interpreter_cache dump in SKILL.md:94.

findings.what: The revision form adds a \revision callout, an Appendix I \subsection with \seclabel, an edit of preamble.tex, and \secref cross-references. The file never says how to build the specification (draft or release), whether the worker must build it to check its LaTeX, or where \revision is defined. Line 11 mentions 'A draft build' and 'a release build' without a command. toolchain.md:7 says only that setup.sh installs LaTeX.
findings.consequence: The spec worker either commits LaTeX it never compiled, where a broken \seclabel/\secref or an undefined macro is caught by no gate (the gate reads only ProjectFortress, Library and build.xml), or it searches Specification/ for a Makefile or latexmk recipe and spends time.

findings.what: 'If a decision of the curator says which side is correct, change the other side to agree.' 'If the passage has an Appendix I entry, add the conflict's ledger row to the departures that its effect lists.' tests-writing.md:83 says a deferred defect that 'the specification settles' gets 'a gated XXX test ... in the change that measured the defect'. SKILL.md:160 says 'An edit of the specification ... has no test', and SKILL.md:52 says building happens in one area at a time.
findings.consequence: After a decision, the spec worker revises the text, and the new text now departs from walk or the compiled path. One reading sends it to change the implementation ('the other side'), crossing areas. Another makes it owe an XXX test in ProjectFortress/tests. A third has it write only a ledger row. The skill does not say which, so the worker guesses or crosses into another area. 'departures that its effect lists' is never defined.

findings.what: worktrees.md:12 says 'Any other run compiles into the caches that every worktree is seeded from', and line 34 says 'Every compile rewrites cache files of the tree that it runs in. So compile only into caches that no other agent compiles into.' build-and-caches.md:23 says 'Walk runs the phases on each component that a run needs. It needs no compile.'
findings.consequence: 'compile' means both 'fortress compile' and any run that writes cache entries, walk included. A library worker under walk reads build-and-caches.md, decides walk 'needs no compile', and runs walk in a shared tree or in the base build. That writes into caches other agents read or seed from. It is also unclear when a walk-only worker 'need[s] a build of your own' and must seed a worktree.

findings.what: 'If a rule of the language or the checker refuses the way that you want, find how the library writes that kind of thing.' interpreter.md:20 says 'No command checks them for a walk program: fortress typecheck checks against the compiler's prelude.' SKILL.md:73 says the switch-over comes 'when the checker accepts the interpreter's library'.
findings.consequence: A worker editing the interpreter's library cannot run the checker on its edit, so it cannot learn that the checker refuses its design. It also does not know whether its edit must keep the library checker-clean for the switch-over. It may spend time trying 'bin/fortress typecheck Library/X.fss', which runs against the wrong prelude and reports spurious errors. Or it may land a design the checker will reject.

findings.what: library.md never sends a library worker to interpreter.md. What a library edit can trigger is there: walk's load-time refusals ('So a library edit that adds an overload can stop every program at load', line 29), the refusal of 'f[\T extends Any\](x: T)' (line 26), and natives bound by builtinPrimitive with classes in interpreter/glue/prim/ (line 35). SKILL.md:197 gives a part list for an interpreter fix but none for a library edit.
findings.consequence: A library worker adds an overload or writes an explicit 'extends Any' bound, and every program then fails to load. Or it adds a native, which is a Java edit under interpreter/, without knowing that this triggers ant compileAll and a full ant testSystem (tests-running.md:61-63). It discovers the rules only after the failure.

findings.what: '$L close N --commit HASH --test NAME marks row N FIXED ... Run it once that commit is in HEAD.' committing.md:11 says 'Commit what you write to the record, such as a ledger row, with the work that it records.'
findings.consequence: A walk fixer who closes the row for its defect cannot do both. The fix commit's hash is not known until the fix is committed, so the close needs a second commit, which committing.md:11 seems to forbid. The worker either pre-commits and amends, breaking the hash, or hesitates over which rule wins.

findings.what: 'an interpreter fix needs build-and-caches.md, session.md, interpreter.md, tests-writing.md, tests-running.md and committing.md.' The list omits worktrees.md, which tests-writing.md:91 needs for running old code and which says whether to seed a worktree. It also omits compiler.md, which interpreter.md:65 requires for the report and for where a fix goes.
findings.consequence: A walk fixer who trusts the example list does not load worktrees.md or compiler.md. It stalls at 'see it fail on the base's code' when its tree already holds an edit, and misses the evaluator-versus-desugarer rule and the two-paths report line.

findings.what: The commit footer must be used 'exactly, whatever footer Claude Code suggests': 'Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>' plus a hard-coded 'Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01AmiXNpJxQ6TBwec4vJZHDB'. Then: 'If the work moves to another session, explorations/protocol.md gives the new session line.'
findings.consequence: A worker whose harness supplies a different Co-Authored-By line, or which runs in another session, cannot tell whether 'moves to another session' covers it. It either uses a session URL that is not its own or opens protocol.md, which is a search.

findings.what: 'A decision of the curator enters POSITIONS in the next commit after the curator states it.' It does not say who writes it. specification.md:47 lets an Appendix I entry cite 'the decision of the curator that it follows (its POSITIONS entry), or the reason that your brief gives'.
findings.consequence: A spec worker revising text right after a decision may think it owes the POSITIONS entry in its own commit. It may write the curator's words into POSITIONS itself, a file other agents also edit, or cite an entry that does not exist yet.

findings.what: 'The full reasoning, in a decision record under explorations/'. The example lives at explorations/compile-ladder/rung-spec-route-a/decision-record.md. records.md:76 says 'If you add a standalone note there, write its INDEX line.' Neither file gives the folder or file name for a new record, or the form of an INDEX line.
findings.consequence: The spec worker invents a location and name, and copies an INDEX line's form by opening INDEX.md, which costs a search. The records end up scattered.

findings.what: Line 31: 'The library's practice gives the design, not the specification's text alone.' Line 33: 'If the library's practice and the specification's text disagree, do as specification.md, "When the text and an implementation disagree", says', and that section treats an undecided disagreement as a conflict that requires exploring.
findings.consequence: Line 31 reads as 'follow practice over the text'. Line 33 reads as 'stop and explore'. A library worker who meets a disagreement may silently follow practice when it should have switched to exploring and filed a conflict.

findings.what: Under 'Compiled': 'library_tests/: the compiler's library.' tests-running.md:17 calls the track that runs it 'library'. Everywhere in library.md, 'the library' means the interpreter's library.
findings.consequence: A worker editing Library/*.fss who skims for 'library' may put its test in library_tests/, which is compiled, links against the compiler's library and needs a .test file. The test then never exercises its walk edit.

findings.what: SKILL.md states without qualification: 'A type parameter that a call does not fix takes its bound.' revival-changes.md:68: 'Under walk, a parameter whose bound names the parameter itself, such as SUM's, still gets Bottom (ledger row 424).'
findings.consequence: A library worker designing a generic with a self-referential bound (an algebra trait like AdditiveGroup[\T\]) relies on SKILL.md's rule and gets Bottom under walk. library.md:25 gives only the SUM-specific workaround.

findings.what: 'run all the tests that it reaches. Run them once for each code state, after your last edit of code.'
findings.consequence: This reads two ways: run after every code state (every edit), or only once after the last edit. A walk fixer might run ant testSystem after each intermediate edit, at several minutes each. The next sub-bullet also says 'For walk, run ant testSystem', which skips misc-track unit tests that may cover the edited interpreter class even though they are 'tests that it reaches'.

findings.what: 'Check an edit of prose in Specification/ or Documentation/ against the tree and the curator's decisions.' This is the only check that applies to a spec edit. It sits in tests-writing.md, which a spec worker has little reason to load ('An edit of the specification ... has no test'), and 'against the tree' does not say how.
findings.consequence: A spec worker misses the check, or is unsure whether it must run programs to confirm the revised sentence. SKILL.md:158 'Reproduce a behaviour before you explain it' suggests it must.

findings.what: SKILL.md: 'At the switch-over ... the compiler's own library is deleted.' compiler.md:39: 'The record does not yet say what happens to CompilerSystem at the switch-over.' library.md:5 counts CompilerSystem as part of the compiler's library.
findings.consequence: A library worker may treat CompilerSystem as disposable, or as settled, when the record leaves it open.

findings.what: The direct-run recipe is 'cd ProjectFortress && ../bin/fortress -debug stacktrace tests/X.fss'. interpreter.md runs from the tree root ('bin/fortress ProjectFortress/tests/BooleanOps.fss'), and name resolution searches '.' first (build-and-caches.md:72).
findings.consequence: A walk fixer who runs from different directories gets different import resolution: a file in ProjectFortress/ can hide a library file of the same name. Its reproduction may then differ from the harness's.

findings.what: 'Start each Bash call that runs Fortress, ant or a project tool with these lines'. 'project tool' is not defined. facts-extract.sh and ledger.py are run by relative path from the tree root.
findings.consequence: A spec worker that runs only facts-extract.sh cannot tell whether it needs the JDK/FORTRESS_HOME setup. If it skips the cd, the relative tool paths fail.

findings.what: The query uses the form 'map:design-intent-sources.md#The map, by design area@WORD'. records.md:62 documents 'map:FILE#HEADING' but not the '@WORD' row filter, which compiler.md:110 and toolchain.md:9 also use.
findings.consequence: The worker infers the syntax, or runs --help.

findings.what: Line 8 says Library/incomplete/ is unreachable: 'Before you cite a declaration as the library's way, check that a running program can reach it.' Line 34 then tells the worker to follow 'the team's proposal (Library/incomplete/Collection.fss)' when a family shows no practice.
findings.consequence: This mildly contradicts line 8. A worker may doubt whether the fallback is allowed.

findings.what: Step 1's callout '\revision{<label>}{...}' uses '<label>', which is 'the \seclabel of the change's Appendix I entry', and that entry is created only in step 2.
findings.consequence: A worker who follows the steps in order writes the callout before the label exists and has to come back. This is minor.

findings.what: 'They leave out env.sh's removal of old parser directories in /tmp. That removal spares the directory of a live run.'
findings.consequence: The second sentence reads as a reason to keep the removal, not to leave it out. A worker cannot tell whether removing /tmp/fortress*rats itself is safe, and gate.md:30 warns that it can break live runs.

findings.what: The parts list names references/build-and-caches.md twice ('Setting up each call' and 'Building, the caches, what to rebuild'). In the file itself, 'Setting up each call' is near the end (line 78), after the sections that assume it.
findings.consequence: A worker loads the file once but may act on the cache and build sections before reaching the setup lines. This is minor.

assumptions.assumed: Which tree a worker works in (<tree>), and whether it must seed its own worktree, is set by its brief. Without a brief, the main checkout /home/user/fortress.
assumptions.why: The setup lines start with 'cd <tree>', and worktrees.md:34 says 'Your brief says where you work'. None of the three walks can start without a tree.

assumptions.assumed: Unqualified Java paths (interpreter/, compiler/, runtimeSystem/, nativeHelpers/, useful/, repository/, parser/, scala_src/) are under ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/, including scala_src/.
assumptions.why: To find Evaluator.java, EvaluatorBase.java and glue/prim/Int.java for the walk fix. SKILL.md:56 states the rule, but scala_src's place comes from CLAUDE.md's '.../scala_src/'.
assumptions.source: skill (SKILL.md:56) plus prior knowledge of the Fortress repo layout

assumptions.assumed: For a walk-only Java fix, the library order (the compiled path's five compiles) need not run after ant compileAll empties default_repository/caches, and leaving the caches empty is acceptable.
assumptions.why: build-and-caches.md:113 ties the library order to 'the next compiled run'. It does not say whether a walk worker must leave its tree's caches warm for others.

assumptions.assumed: How to build the specification (a Makefile or latexmk in Specification/) and that \revision, \seclabel and \secref are macros already defined in the spec's style files.

the Meet Rule for Functional Methods, the Return Type Rule, the exclusion rule: named and cited but stated only loosely (SKILL.md:123-125, interpreter.md:25).

findings.what: SKILL.md:50 says the explorer "add[s] what you found to the record", but exploring.md step 6 sends every finding only to tests-writing.md "How a defect is recorded" (a test plus a ledger row). Nothing in exploring.md covers a finding that is not a defect: a fact about the original tree, a source that settles a conflict, or a FACTS line that is wrong. The routes for those are in records.md:73-76 ("Add a fact to FACTS in the commit that establishes it", a note under explorations/ with an INDEX line), but exploring.md never points there. records.md also does not say whether a worker may write FACTS, which FACTS section a new entry goes in, or what test a fact needs (SKILL.md:137 says "Each fact has its source and its test"). It gives no tool for FACTS, while the ledger has ledger.py.
findings.consequence: An explorer whose finding is not a defect either files it wrongly as a ledger row, leaves it only in the report so the record never gets it, or edits FACTS by hand with no format, section or test, and possibly without permission. Then it searches records.md and INDEX to work out which of these was meant.

findings.what: "A decision of the curator enters POSITIONS in the next commit after the curator states it" and "Rewrite a wrong line of FACTS or POSITIONS in place" read as instructions to any worker. Elsewhere POSITIONS holds only the curator's words: records.md:75, SKILL.md:155, and exploring.md:18 ("If you have evidence against a decision ... read its POSITIONS entry") with step 10 (report it as a decision not taken).
findings.consequence: An explorer that finds a POSITIONS line contradicted by evidence can read line 74 as permission to rewrite the curator's decision in place, when it should report a decision not taken. A worker whose brief quotes a curator ruling can also think it must write that ruling into POSITIONS itself.

findings.what: "The parts, in the order that work meets them" lists the setup lines first and toolchain.md fifth, as "The build failing, JDKs". The setup lines hard-code JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-25-openjdk-amd64. toolchain.md:3 says the container's profile has JDK 21, and toolchain.md:7 gives the apt-get install of JDK 25 and ant. The setup section has no check that JDK 25 or ant is present.
findings.consequence: On a fresh machine the worker exports a JAVA_HOME that does not exist and runs ant compileAll (often as a backgrounded 200 s job). It sees the failure, and only then finds the install line in a part it was told it would meet later. That costs a build cycle and a search.

findings.what: Step 4 is only "Search the original tree." SKILL.md:189 promises that exploring.md tells "where to search", but it names no tool or place. The aids are scattered: the feature table and phase map are in compiler.md:106-114, the design-intent map and the \note{} grep in specification.md:11,27-31, and git history and authorship in records.md:94-100. exploring.md links none of them.
findings.consequence: The explorer greps blindly through Java, Scala, LaTeX and Fortress. It misses the maps that name the spec section, parser rule, checker class, walk site and ledger rows of a feature, and it misses the \note{} boxes that already say a feature was not built. It may also miss the cut parent links in git history (records.md:99) and conclude wrongly from `git log` of a directory.

findings.what: The section covers only making a new seeded worktree with seed-worktree.sh <base-build> <new-worktree> <branch>. It does not cover a worker that starts inside a fresh worktree, whether unbuilt or already seeded by someone else. It does not say whether to seed into the current path (line 42 hints that an existing worktree is accepted), what <branch> to pass then, or whether to make another worktree and move. A worker in a worktree that someone else seeded never saw the script's list of library sources that differ (line 43) or its warning that "the copied build is the base's" (line 44), and no command is given to recompute either.
findings.consequence: A worker in a fresh, unbuilt worktree runs ant compileAll there, which the skill says to avoid ("seed ... instead of building"). Or it seeds a second worktree and leaves its starting one, or passes a wrong branch. A worker in a pre-seeded worktree skips a needed library recompile and gets stale-jar symptoms (NoSuchMethodError) on its first compiled run.

findings.what: The base-build recipe needs <base-commit>. The skill defines the base only as "Commit that your work starts from" (SKILL.md:37) and gives a fallback (merge-base) only for checking a fix (line 30). The recipe is printed as plain foreground commands: ant compileAll, the five-compile library order (100-110 s) and a walk run. Together these take about 200 s, longer than the Bash tool's 120 s limit, and the recipe does not mention run_bg.
findings.consequence: On a fresh machine, with a brief that names no base, the worker guesses the commit (HEAD, origin/main or its branch point). It may also run the block in one foreground call, where the command is killed or moved to the background and leaves a half-built base build. seed-worktree.sh then refuses that base build, or worse, accepts it.

findings.what: wait_for is described as printing "the log's verdict lines", but it greps only '^BUILD ', '^Total time:' and '^EXIT='. harness-one.sh, junit.sh and fortress junit end with JUnit's "OK (n tests)" or "FAILURES!!!" and exit 0 whatever the verdict (tests-running.md:83).
findings.consequence: A test-only worker that runs junit.sh or harness-one.sh under run_bg sees only EXIT=0 from wait_for and can take a failing run as passing, unless it remembers to grep the log for OK or FAILURES.

findings.what: Step 6 records the finding, "for an open question" by item 3: a test of today's behaviour plus a ledger row, which treats the defect as deferred. Steps 9-10, which decide whether the choice is the worker's to make or the curator's, come later.
findings.consequence: An explorer whose choice turns out to be its own (step 9: make it) has already written an item-3 test that pins the wrong behaviour, and a ledger row. Making the choice should instead give an item-1 assertion with no row, so the explorer must undo or rewrite what it recorded.

findings.what: "The curator settles the question after research" contradicts exploring.md:7-12 and step 9, under which some exploration questions are the worker's to settle ("If the choice is yours, make it").
findings.consequence: An explorer that reads SKILL.md first sends every question to the curator as a decision not taken, even ones it should settle itself. Or, seeing the conflict, it cannot tell which file rules.

findings.what: The rules assume every test reproduces a defect: "Start with your own failing test", "Write the test before the fix", and "quote two to five lines of the failing run and the passing line". Nothing covers a worker that only adds tests that pass today (coverage, or a regression guard): whether it must show a failure, what it quotes, and whether the test-first order applies when the test file is itself "source code in the original tree".
findings.consequence: A test-only worker either invents failing variants to satisfy the order, or searches for a rule that does not exist. Its report then lacks the evidence expected of it, or carries made-up evidence.

findings.what: The template test program asserts and prints nothing. Line 62, below it, says a compiled run test with no run_out check must output "pass" or "PASS". The template applies to both paths, and the rule to print PASS last appears only under Promoting (line 127).
findings.consequence: A test-only worker that copies the template into compiler_tests/ with link and run keys gets a red run, and must debug why a program with passing asserts fails.

findings.what: Item 3 asks for "a test that asserts today's behaviour". Under walk, a test is green only if it throws no exception (line 40), and a Fortress catch sees no Java exception from a native (interpreter.md:42). So a run-time crash under walk cannot be asserted as today's behaviour. The only escapes are a load-refusal .test file or "If no program can observe the defect", and neither fits.
findings.consequence: An explorer recording a walk crash on an open question writes an XXX test instead (item 2, meant for questions the specification settles), or files a ledger row with reproducer "none" although a program does observe the defect.

findings.what: "also record what specification.md asks for" does not say what that is. specification.md asks for several things: grep the \note{} boxes, cite the .fsi rather than a listing, flag which sources are type-group positions, and add the conflict's ledger row to the departures of the passage's Appendix I entry. The last is an edit of Specification/, part of the original tree, and specification.md:35 says every change of the text needs the four-part revision form.
findings.consequence: The explorer does not know whether it must edit appendices/changes.tex, whether that edit needs a \revision callout and a decision record, or whether its brief even lets it edit the original tree.

findings.what: The section opens "Your brief says whether you run the gate" and then says "If it prints a path, run the gate again." The regex counts as test files only .fss, .fsi and .test files directly in tests/ or *_tests/. A helper api or component in ProjectFortress/test_library/, where tests-writing.md:41 sends it, is therefore not a test file.
findings.consequence: A test-only worker that adds a test_library helper sees the command print a path, and must choose between running a 25-minute gate that its brief did not ask for and ignoring this line.

findings.what: The default "commit on your current branch, and push it" lands work on main without a gate when the current branch is main, although SKILL.md:41 makes the gate the check before landing. For a worker in a seeded worktree on its own branch, no step says how its commits reach main. A worktree cannot check out main while the main tree has it checked out, and the "If you work on main" steps assume it can.
findings.consequence: A fresh-worktree worker whose brief says to land does not know whether to merge, cherry-pick or push branch:main. A worker in the main tree with a silent brief pushes main ungated.

findings.what: POSITIONS and FACTS can be queried only by words of an entry's bold title (and FACTS by section heading). There is no query over their content. The skill does not say whether grepping the files is allowed, although line 49 forbids reading the ledger whole and exploring.md:3 warns that workers called things absent that the record held.
findings.consequence: An explorer whose topic is not in a title gets no match and concludes the record is silent, which is the exact error exploring.md warns about. Otherwise it greps the files without knowing whether it may.

findings.what: A new ledger row needs one of seven status words: POSITIVE-VERIFIED, NEGATIVE-VERIFIED, NEGATIVE-BOUNDED, CONTESTED and three closing words. The skill defines none of them and says nothing about which one a new open question takes.
findings.consequence: The explorer must print the 3 KB template and guess, possibly marking a conflict that only the curator can settle with one of the VERIFIED words instead of CONTESTED.

findings.what: Step 7 covers only "If your brief does not let you edit the ledger". No part says what a silent brief allows. committing.md:6 sets a default for committing, but no default exists for ledger or FACTS edits.
findings.consequence: With a silent brief, an explorer either writes the ledger and may collide with the coordinator, or puts the row only in its report so the record does not get it.

findings.what: $T is defined as old-fortress.sh here and as facts-extract.sh in records.md:55. Both are used in single Bash calls.
findings.consequence: A worker that defines both in one call, for example to check the ledger and then reproduce on the old code, runs one tool with the other's arguments.

findings.what: "climb-batch-N is the folder's real name, not a placeholder", but gate.md:9 uses climb-batch-<N> as a placeholder, and the gate-summary glob climb-batch-* matches numbered folders.
findings.consequence: A test-only worker looking for junit.sh may substitute a number, or doubt the literal path, and lose time listing folders.

findings.what: "Before you edit a file of the original tree, list the ledger rows that cite it" sits inside "Reading the record". It is absent from SKILL.md's rules and from tests-writing.md. SKILL.md:194 tells workers to load records.md for reports, not before edits.
findings.consequence: A test-only worker that respells a line of a team test (tests-writing.md:135), or an explorer adding a test, edits files cited by ledger rows without seeing those rows.

findings.what: "If your change touches mutable state, a field, an atomic block ... run its checks at one thread and at four." Almost every object test touches a field.
findings.consequence: A test-only worker either reruns every new test directly at one thread, which costs time, or must decide which tests count. The line does not say whether adding a test that uses a var is "a change that touches mutable state".

findings.what: setup.sh is offered beside the apt-get line. It "builds the tree and sets up the transcript backup", with no word on which tree or whether a worker should run it.
findings.consequence: A fresh-machine worker may run setup.sh. That builds the main tree into the caches other agents use, and arms a backup that belongs to the cloud-container skill.

findings.what: Two different remedies for having no clean, built base build. Lines 16-21 say to build a base build, then seed from it. Line 41, for seed exit 2, says to make the worktree with git worktree add and build it yourself.
findings.consequence: A fresh-machine worker may build its working tree directly. Every later worker on that machine then finds no base build and repeats the 200 s build.

findings.what: After the seeding warning, the instruction is "run ant compileAll, then the library order" with no condition. build-and-caches.md says to run the library order only after a build that printed "started again, empty" or after certain .fsi edits.
findings.consequence: A worker may spend 100-110 s on an unneeded library order, or skip it when it is needed.

findings.what: The base-build recipe runs bin/fortress ProjectFortress/tests/BooleanOps.fss inside the base build and then requires git status --porcelain to print nothing. Line 62 says "a program writes its own logs beside it".
findings.consequence: If those logs are not gitignored, the base build is never clean and seed-worktree.sh refuses it. The worker then has to debug the recipe.

findings.what: The commit footer hard-codes one Claude-Session URL and says "If the work moves to another session, explorations/protocol.md gives the new session line". It does not say how a worker tells that it runs in another session.
findings.consequence: Workers in other sessions stamp commits with a wrong session link.

findings.what: "Cite the specification by file and section or entry, never by line" is phrased generally. records.md asks for spec sentences "quoted with its file and line", and Appendix I entries quote frozen text "with its path and line".
findings.consequence: An explorer may drop line numbers from report citations, or a test writer may put them in tests. Low cost, but the two rules read as contradictory.

findings.what: "If your tree has no build, build it first (worktrees.md for a new worktree)" conflicts with worktrees.md:34, which says to seed instead of building.
findings.consequence: A worker in an unbuilt tree runs ant compileAll in place.

findings.what: "For a refusal at compile time, write one XXX compile test" does not name which key asserts the refusal, compile_err_contains or compile_exception_contains. The next line names the key only for a code-generator wall, and line 75 warns that compile_err_contains on a program that compiles gives red.
findings.consequence: A test-only worker guesses the key and may write an XXX test that turns green or red for the wrong reason.

findings.what: "each source, and its date" gives no way to date a source: the specification's chapters, papers, library lines or implementation code.
findings.consequence: The explorer works out a dating method itself, such as git log --follow, the paper's year or the frozen draft's date, and must report it as a command it worked out.

findings.what: The example says an interpreter fix needs build-and-caches, session, interpreter, tests-writing, tests-running and committing. It leaves out worktrees.md, which tests-writing step 2 needs for old-fortress.sh, and records.md, which holds the ledger checks before an edit.
findings.consequence: A worker that loads exactly the example's list misses the old-code procedure and the ledger --cites check.

findings.what: "If you add a standalone note there, write its INDEX line" gives neither the form of an INDEX line nor what counts as a standalone note as against a report file.
findings.consequence: An explorer that adds a note opens INDEX to copy its form, or skips the line.

assumptions.assumed: facts-extract.sh, ledger.py, seed-worktree.sh, harness-one.sh and junit.sh are run with the current directory at the tree root, because their paths are relative
assumptions.why: Every query and tool in records.md, worktrees.md and tests-running.md is written as a relative path, and only the setup lines' `cd <tree>` makes them resolve

assumptions.assumed: The base commit comes from the brief, or else is origin/main's HEAD
assumptions.why: worktrees.md's base-build recipe needs <base-commit>, and SKILL.md defines the base only as the commit the work starts from

assumptions.assumed: A worker may edit FACTS.md and INDEX.md directly with the Edit tool, choosing a section by topic
assumptions.why: records.md says to add facts to FACTS and INDEX lines for notes, but gives a tool only for the ledger

assumptions.assumed: CONTESTED is the status for a new row on a question that only the curator can settle, and the *-VERIFIED and NEGATIVE-BOUNDED words mean a verified present or absent gap
assumptions.why: An explorer's new ledger row must carry one of the seven undefined status words

assumptions.assumed: seed-worktree.sh can target an existing, unbuilt worktree path, keeping its branch
assumptions.why: To walk a worker that starts inside a fresh worktree; line 42's 'If the worktree already has a build, the script keeps it' hints at this

assumptions.assumed: A test that passes today needs no failing run, only a green run through the harness, quoted in the report
assumptions.why: The test-only worker's walk; the skill's test order covers only defects

assumptions.assumed: A compiled run test prints PASS with println("PASS") as its last line
assumptions.why: Line 62 requires PASS output, and the template program prints nothing; println appears only in an error message example (fortress.CompilerBuiltin.println)
assumptions.source: guess from the error example and prior knowledge of print functions

assumptions.assumed: apt-get runs as root and reaches the package mirrors through the proxy on a fresh machine
assumptions.why: toolchain.md's install line is the only way to get JDK 25 and ant
assumptions.source: prior knowledge of the cloud container

assumptions.assumed: python3 and git (with a commit identity) are installed on a fresh machine
assumptions.why: ledger.py, the classify.py-based scripts and every commit need them; the skill never says to install them

assumptions.assumed: The main clone is at /home/user/fortress on a fresh machine
assumptions.why: worktrees.md hard-codes `git -C /home/user/fortress worktree add`

assumptions.assumed: Variables exported by the setup lines reach the command that run_bg starts with nohup bash -c, so the setup lines go in the same Bash call before run_bg
assumptions.why: session.md defines run_bg separately from the setup lines and does not say they must be combined

assumptions.assumed: Under wait_for, the verdict of harness-one.sh or junit.sh must be grepped from the log separately (OK (n tests) or FAILURES!!!)
assumptions.why: wait_for prints only BUILD, Total time and EXIT lines, and those scripts exit 0 whatever the verdict

assumptions.assumed: 'Search the original tree' means grep over ProjectFortress/src, Library, Specification and Papers, plus git log --follow and the map notes named in compiler.md and specification.md
assumptions.why: exploring.md step 4 gives no method
assumptions.source: prior knowledge plus assembling other parts

assumptions.assumed: The branch name for a new seeded worktree comes from the brief, and a seeded worktree cannot be on main while the main tree is
assumptions.why: seed-worktree.sh needs <branch>, and committing.md's main-push steps assume main is checked out
assumptions.source: prior knowledge of git worktrees; guess for the naming

assumptions.assumed: A walk run's logs beside a program are gitignored, so the base build stays clean after the BooleanOps warm-up run
assumptions.why: The base-build recipe requires git status --porcelain to print nothing after that run

assumptions.assumed: Writing a ledger row and FACTS entries counts as editing the record, not the original tree, so a brief that forbids original-tree edits still allows them unless it says otherwise
assumptions.why: tests-writing.md:86 and exploring.md:22 give separate permissions for the original tree and the ledger
assumptions.source: inference from SKILL.md:17's definition of the original tree

assumptions.assumed: The Bash tool's timeout parameter is in milliseconds, and the agent's prompt cache is the reason for the 270 s cap
assumptions.why: To follow session.md's long-command procedure
assumptions.source: session.md plus prior knowledge of the tool

assumptions.assumed: A FACTS entry's 'test' may be a command and its output when no gated test exists
assumptions.why: FACTS entries need a source and a test, and an explorer's facts about the team's sources often have no program

assumptions.assumed: In this environment the commit footer is the one committing.md gives, not the Co-Authored-By line the session's system reminder suggests
assumptions.why: The two footers differ; committing.md says 'exactly, whatever footer Claude Code suggests'
assumptions.source: the skill's own wording, plus the precedence the reminder grants project instructions

terms: green: a tree whose suites passed (SKILL.md:162), the gate passing (gate.md:3), and the harness's report on a test (tests-writing.md:6), which for an XXX test means it fails. SKILL.md uses the word before tests-writing.md defines it
red: a failing test, a passing XXX test, and a failing gate
tree: the 'original tree' (what the team left, SKILL.md:16) and a 'tree' (a checkout, build-and-caches.md:3). Both are used in the same sentences ('Search the original tree', 'your tree's tmp/')
